# Anti-Generic Alternatives

When a default pattern is detected, removing it is half the job. This map gives genuinely different
alternatives for each common default, drawn from the composition and direction libraries and from
observed precedent. The anti-slop procedure picks **at least three alternatives from different
families**, compares them, and chooses by context. Keeping the original is allowed when it has a
stated job (see the justified-trends precedent).

| Default detected | Its usual (missing) job | Alternatives from different families | Precedent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Centered card on a blank page | Frame a focused task | Environment-first focus; asymmetric split with real context; dominant object (the product's own input); poster statement for an event | Kahoot KH1, ChatGPT CG1, Cursor CU1, Framer FR1 |
| Giant hero + two CTAs + tilted screenshot | Explain and persuade | Product-first hero (live widget); workbench tour; stat-led with a real number; long document; poster statement | Wise W1, MDN MD3, Stripe SR2, Patagonia PA1 |
| Four KPI cards on a dashboard | Tell the user what matters | Action-first dashboard (exceptions, changes, owners); status-row list; data investigation with saved views | GitHub Actions GA1, Bloomberg BL1 |
| Every feature in a card grid / bento | Present several capabilities | Sticky feature stack; split narrative with proof; ranked list with one deep feature; diagram of the system | Datadog DD2, Slack SL2 |
| Fake-premium whitespace | Pacing and emphasis | Scale the focal object; editorial rhythm with real content; environment with a product motif; tighten and add real state | Apple AP2, Vercel VC1, Brilliant BR1 |
| Purple-blue gradient everywhere | Brand energy | Signature field used once (environment only); product-derived color from the product's object; typographic voice; photography | Stripe SR3, Monzo MZ1, Wise W4 |
| Glass panels over a gradient | Depth and layering | Solid surfaces with value steps; real overlay over real content; layered depth with product imagery | Revolut RV1, Discord DI3 |
| Pills for every label | Friendliness, grouping | Plain text metadata; small caps labels; pills only for filters/tokens; status icon + text | GitHub GA1 |
| Segmented / animated code input | Make the task feel special | Standard input in a branded environment; big legible type in a plain field; paste support | Kahoot KH2, Blooket BK1 |
| Tiny uppercase grey eyebrows | Section labeling, polish | Stronger heading scale; two-tone headline; numbered sections in a real editorial system | Stripe SR1, The Guardian GU3 |
| Generic icons on every item | Scannability | Remove repeated icons; product-specific icon set; typographic lists; real thumbnails | The Pudding PU3, Coursera CO2 |
| Fade/slide on every element | Liveliness | Event-driven motion on real changes; a single meaningful entrance; stillness | Apple HIG AHM1, Material MDT2 |
| Command palette in a small app | Speed for experts | Keyboard shortcuts on visible buttons; good search; contextual menus | Grafana GF4 (palette where scope justifies it) |
| Bottom sheets for everything (mobile) | Contextual options | Direct controls on the item; inline menus; native pickers | Airbnb ABm1–ABm4 |
| Generic AI copy ("Unlock…") | Persuasion | Specific, checkable claims; a live number; the product working | Wise W5, Arc AR1, Cloudflare CF1 |
| Dark "developer" aesthetic by default | Technical credibility | Real code and docs structure; light technical monochrome; a product-derived carrier | MDN MD1, Stripe Docs SD1 |
| Decorative illustration filling empty space | Warmth, fullness | Real content or state; a proportionate spot illustration in a real empty state; a pattern in the environment | Spotify SPd1, Grafana GF2 |

## Procedure

1. **Name the default** and the job it was (probably) trying to do.
2. **Check justification:** does it have a stated job here (see justified trends)? If yes, keep it and
   make it serve that job better.
3. **Generate three alternatives** from different rows or families above (composition, direction,
   content). Write one sentence each on how it would look for *this* product.
4. **Compare** against the product's archetype, content available, and constraints.
5. **Choose and derive:** replace generic parts with product-specific content and motifs.
6. **Verify:** logo test, anti-slop gate, render at real sizes and states.
